criteria.statement: Repository, remote, default branch, and project identity are ChangeBridge only.
The verified predecessor commit/tree and Stage 2 checkpoint match exactly.
Part 1 and Part 2 Stage 1/2 frozen validators pass.
Protected predecessor evidence digests remain unchanged.
Concurrent-edit and overlapping-PR review is clear or explicitly resolved.
The Stage 3 authority conflict is recorded and corrected without dropping work.
Stage 3 scope, non-goals, write surface, dependencies, and claims are frozen.
Machine-readable requirements, contracts, reason codes, and evidence schema agree.
A clean disposable environment installs only authorized dependencies and artifacts.
Python, Java, Spark, Scala, and Iceberg form one proven compatibility matrix.
Every external runtime artifact has recorded provenance and SHA-256.
Spark local mode creates, commits, reads, and inspects a real Iceberg table.
Iceberg commit metadata exposes the stable token required for recovery.
CI runs the real target and cannot convert missing prerequisites into success.
Generation identity is deterministic and bound to accepted lineage.
Each generation has a distinct warehouse, namespace, and table map.
The control store durably records generation, shard, commit, transition, and proof state.
CREATED to SNAPSHOT_LOADING is expected-revision guarded and idempotent.
Writes to protected or foreign generations fail before mutation.
Iceberg schemas derive from accepted contracts with explicit type mappings.
Governed metadata binds generation, source, contract, schema, snapshot, and S.
The physical table map and Iceberg snapshot identities are durably receipted.
Path traversal, symlink escape, and namespace aliasing are rejected.
The complete accepted pre-boundary state reconstructs as six orders and 66 order items with matching digests.
The full handoff passes the unchanged Stage 2 normalizer; only snapshot records at S are loaded and post-S CDC is preserved.
Real Spark loads all 72 accepted snapshot rows into generation-scoped Iceberg tables.
Every shard follows a durable claimed, staged, committed, reconciled lifecycle.
Identical shard replay returns the prior result without a new Iceberg snapshot.
Conflicting replay of one shard identity fails closed.
Duplicate keys, incomplete or altered input, wrong schema, and wrong lineage are rejected.
A partial shard set remains SNAPSHOT_LOADING and cannot admit CDC.
Pre-commit faults leave no acknowledged target commit and recover safely.
Post-Iceberg/pre-ledger failure recovers from durable metadata without rewrite.
Post-ledger/pre-transition ambiguity reconciles idempotently.
Source and target table and generation counts match at S.
Canonical keyed-row digests and schemas match the independent snapshot oracle.
Active and foreign generation logical and physical identities remain unchanged.
SNAPSHOT_LOADING to CDC_APPLYING occurs only after a complete immutable admission receipt passes.
The full suite and real Spark/Iceberg CI pass on the exact reviewed PR head and tree.
The guarded merge succeeds only for the expected reviewed head under repository policy.
Fresh merged main preserves the reviewed tree and passes clean-room verification.
The external PART2_STAGE3_SNAPSHOT_GENERATION_VERIFIED checkpoint records exact identities, evidence digests, limitations, and Stage 4 entry.
